positions.assessment: The board is FAM, Assault Dragon and Dark Armed Dragon against an empty opponent. Dark Armed Dragon has no useful target, and using it would hit my own cards. Setting Delta Crow costs nothing. FAM is a Blackwing, so Delta Crow works, and it will be live on the opponent's turn.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: Setting Delta Crow adds backup against their Set Spells/Traps. Ending without setting would gain nothing, and Dark Armed Dragon's effect would only hit my own cards.

positions.assessment: Simoon's effect is already on the chain and Black Whirlwind is placed. Normal Summoning Simoon for free triggers Black Whirlwind to search, and it doesn't use my own Normal Summon. Sending Simoon to the GY gains nothing, since one Simoon is already there.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: The free Normal Summon starts the Black Whirlwind search chain (Sudri next) and keeps the real Normal Summon. The opponent's Set cards might include a Solemn Strike, but the other option gives up the engine anyway.

positions.assessment: Ahrima is stuck: its effect was used this turn, and Blue-Eyes Alternative will destroy it next turn. Enemy Controller can Tribute Ahrima, which would be lost anyway, to take Alternative and hit for 3000. That also empties my board for a Simoon turn next time, with Chinook as the banish cost. The opponent has a Set card, so a negation is possible. Setting Controller for their turn gains little, because stealing in response only lasts until the End Phase and I can't attack with it then.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: It turns a doomed Ahrima into 3000 damage and clears the board for next turn's Simoon. The steal is only temporary, but the damage is real and the cost is minimal.

grades.label: B
grades.reason: Holding Controller for their turn is passive. A response steal only lasts until the End Phase with no attack, so Ahrima is lost for little. It does avoid a possible negation of the 3000-damage play, and the reasoning about Chinook is sound.
